claim_summary: SwingGuard contributes a feedback-driven decision-support runtime that conditions daily trading proposals on point-in-time risk and governs executed exposure through a persistent five-minute controller.

claim_evidence.quote: SwingGuard, a dual-timescale, long-only multi-agent framework for risk-conditioned strategy generation.
a five-minute Risk Controller performs conditional diagnosis, maintains persistent risk states with staged recovery

modules.name: Point-in-time evidence preparation
modules.scope_reason: The mechanism aligns time-indexed evidence under an availability cutoff without encoding a trading output requirement, so it meets R3_2_GTS. If the task family changed, source adapters could change while point-in-time availability semantics remain reusable.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:no - source alignment does not encode a task output objective or trading verifier
R3_2_GTS:yes - point-in-time temporal availability is core
R8:inferred - one task family, temporal interface generalizes

evidence.quote: The deterministic Data Team aligns point-in-time sources
All decision inputs obey a point-in-time availability boundary.

modules.name: Risk-conditioned multi-agent strategy generation
modules.scope_reason: The procedure forms long-only trading targets and execution parameters under a trading risk context, embedding the decision_support output objective (R3_1_TSK). A different task family would require redesigning its trading target, sizing, stops, and risk constraints.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - it forms a trading target and executable parameters under trading constraints

evidence.quote: Full SwingGuard supplies Rd,0 to both internal stages, so the risk state can alter the direction, feasible size, and parameters considered before finalization.

modules.name: Five-minute risk diagnosis and persistent state governance
modules.scope_reason: The diagnosis and state machine produce trading exposure caps and staged recovery actions, embedding the trading objective (R3_1_TSK). If the task family changed, risk states, exposure actions, and their verifier would need redesign; its five-minute windows and earlier-snapshot cutoff are temporal functions within that task procedure.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - risk states govern trading exposure and recovery
R4:Memory and Context; Planning and Orchestration

evidence.quote: for every completed five-minute bar, Stage 1 screens market, on-chain, and news anomalies with deterministic rules.
Hysteresis and minimum holds prevent a quiet bar from immediately erasing risk.

modules.name: Hard-boundary trade audit and execution trace
modules.scope_reason: The auditor validates trading direction, size, stops, and validity against controller limits, then maps the approved position to execution, embedding a trading-specific verifier (R3_1_TSK). A different task family would require redesigning the proposal contract and execution actions.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - validates and executes a trading-position contract
R4:Planning and Orchestration; Tools and Execution
R5:task_procedure - no temporal function is implemented by the audit itself

evidence.quote: After proposal generation, a hard-boundary auditor h validates long-only direction, size, stop, validity horizon, and controller limits;
This trace separates the LLM proposal, validated target, state-driven constraint, and realized position, linking risk evidence to execution.

process_validity.quote: At 21:15 on December 18, the controller entered the survival response and closed the 30% exposure.

temporal_validity.quote: All decision inputs obey a point-in-time availability boundary.

decision_utility.quote: The synchronized, cost-adjusted portfolio returns 37.16% with 2.98 Sharpe and 6.44% drawdown, versus 30.11%, 1.19, and 28.47% for equal-weight buy-and-hold.
